headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared write channels or network egress, but ComfyUI’s file-based inputs can still be misused if manually bridged into marker.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can ingest file-based workflows and model assets, while marker has no shared channel or parser surface documented. There is no default direct bridge between them, so prompt injection is not inherent; only manual copy/paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions. The pairwise pathway is therefore unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated text or workflow content into marker as trusted input, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem is used to shuttle untrusted prompt-like content between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste model-generated text into marker without review.
Use a strict file naming convention for handoffs.
Strip instructions from any shared artifacts before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are open-source and show no network egress beyond ComfyUI vendor-only calls and marker none, with no documented shared workspace or credentials. ComfyUI touches local model files; marker touches no data classes here. Leakage is not a default pairwise pathway, but a manual shared-folder setup could expose local assets.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local directory containing sensitive assets, those assets can be exposed through operator handling.
IF ComfyUI is configured to send outputs to an external service, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Store sensitive assets outside any shared workspace.
Disable any optional export or upload integrations.
Review output folders before sharing artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP, so there is no overlapping mutable-resource write surface. ComfyUI’s asynchronous queue and marker’s empty concurrency model do not create a shared lockless write path. The pairwise conflict pathway is effectively blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem write access to the same directory, conflict risk becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, contention can emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid placing them behind a shared mutable workspace.
If writes are added later, introduce file locks.
Run them under separate OS users.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can produce workflows, images, and model artifacts that marker might later process, but marker is a document processor and no default authority chain is documented. Without evidence that marker treats ComfyUI output as authoritative, the cascade is limited to manual workflow mistakes rather than automatic harmful action.
conditions: IF marker is configured to ingest ComfyUI outputs as authoritative source material without verification, downstream errors can cascade.
IF ComfyUI outputs are used to generate documents that marker then republishes, mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Add a human review step between agents.
Require source attribution in marker outputs.
Validate ComfyUI artifacts before ingestion.
Keep generated content clearly labeled as untrusted.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: ComfyUI is offline-capable with vendor-only egress, and marker shows no network egress or sensitive data classes. The profiles do not indicate PHI, EU PII, residency constraints, or retention differences. With only docs-level evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later used on regulated data classes not shown in the profiles, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy imposes residency or retention rules outside these profiles, those rules must be checked separately.
mitigations: Confirm data-class scope before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings.
Review vendor terms for any optional cloud features.
